messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — auth-service-prod: unusual 401 spike (unknown IPs). Severity: P1. Link: https://incidents.redwood/1768644321 :rotating_light:

sam: taking it. oncall here, pinging @maria and @jane for triage.

maria: looking now — tailing auth logs, seeing repeated bearer failures from a small IP range 45.77.12.0/24, starting ~2026-03-20T17:02Z.

maria: snippet from auth-proxy logs (masked):
```
2026-03-20T17:03:12Z auth-proxy[pid=1234] "GET /v1/embeddings" 401 "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***a3f" src=45.77.12.19
2026-03-20T17:03:13Z auth-proxy[pid=1234] "POST /v1/chat" 401 "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_***b7c" src=45.77.12.21
```

maria: those token fragments match a svc-account used by indexer-forwarder. I think debug logs containing long-lived keys were forwarded.

jane: are those user tokens or service tokens? we need to know TTL and impact. @maria can you confirm service account id?

maria: confirmed — svc:svcindexer-prod. Tokens appear in plaintext in a staging -> forwarding pipeline. probable leak path: indexer debug log -> log-forwarder -> external aggregator.

leo: immediate containment suggestions: block the 45.77.12.0/24 at WAF, disable external log-forwarder ingestion, rotate svcindexer-prod keys, revoke any active tokens issued to that service.

sam: action items:
- jane: kick key rotation & legal/cust comms check
- maria: run a focused search for leaked tokens and mark artifacts for quarantine (do not delete raw logs until legal says)
- leo: apply WAF block and disable forwarder streams
- ana: confirm customer-facing errors and open support ticket if needed
I’ll coordinate and update status.

jane: starting key rotation now. creating rotation run in KMS and generating new creds. request id: KR-20260320-91. ETA ~12m to rotate + propagate. I'll also create a security incident ticket and loop legal/comms.

maria: running grep across log buckets for "sk_live_" pattern, excluding already-redacted entries. Marking candidate objects: s3://prod-logs/auth/2026-03-20/part-00012.gz, s3://staging-logs/forwarder/dump-20260320.log. Do not purge yet — preserving for forensics.

leo: WAF rule applied: waf-block-1768644321 (blocks 45.77.12.0/24). Applied at edge. also disabled external-forwarder pipeline: forwarder-prod -> paused.

ana: (note: ana) ana: checking support queue — one customer reported increased 401s around 17:05Z but no data exfil reports yet. opening ticket 8942 and flagging for potential notice.

sre-lead: paste runbook? need steps for rotating service account creds + confirm no cascading failures.

jane: runbook link: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/security/key-rotation. Quick steps executed: revoke old key, create new key, update deployment secrets (k8s secret update), restart pods that read secret.

maria: executed revoke for svcindexer-prod (revoke API call). command I ran:
```
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/keys/revoke" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" -d '{"service":"svcindexer-prod","key_id":"key-9a3f"}'
```

maria: new key issued and pushed to k8s secret svcindexer-creds, restarted indexer pods (rolling). now running scrub job to redact leaked tokens from downstream archive (job id scrub-20260320-7).

jane: KMS rotation shows status: propagated -> 90%. continuing. started customer-comms draft with legal: will hold until containment confirmed.

leo: verified indexer restarted with new creds, no auth failures from internal health checks. WAF blocks in place, forwarder paused.

ana: support ticket 8942 updated: customer saw 401 spikes but nominal service restored after 17:25Z. no reported data loss. marking as monitor.

sam: good. two important notes: 1) keep raw evidence intact for forensics/legal. 2) prepare short internal incident summary for execs once we confirm containment.

jane: agreed. legal asked we do not notify customers publicly until we confirm token scope and whether any external aggregator received data. I'll coordinate with @ana for targeted outreach if needed.

maria: scrub job progress: 40% through listed artifacts, will complete in ~25m. leaving copies in legal-hold bucket.

sre-lead: any followups on CI/CD creds referencing svcindexer-prod? scan results?
maria: quick scan shows two infra scripts used the old key in a maintenance cron; rotating those now and opening PRs to remove plaintext keys.

leo: applied an emergency policy to rate-limit auth requests globally for src=45.77.12.* and related patterns for 1h window.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigation in progress, severity remains P1 until forensic review done.

ana: support: customers flagged: cust-17 and cust-43. notified internal CSMs and created follow-up actions.

sam: staging a short post to #all-hands-infra once legal approves wording. for now status: containment in place, keys rotated, forwarder paused, WAF rules applied, scrub job running.

jane: forensic team requested a copy of preserved logs -> uploaded to secure-evidence/1768644321. audit id AE-20260320-1768.

maria: scrub job complete for identified artifacts. checklist: revoked keys ✅, new keys rolled ✅, forwarder paused ✅, WAF block ✅, evidence preserved ✅.

sam: great work. switching to monitoring mode. assigning follow-ups for postmortem: root-cause on forwarder debug logging, remove any plaintext secrets in pipelines, long-term: rotate expiring service tokens to short-lived ephemeral creds.

jane: will schedule incident review with legal/security/ops tomorrow.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS — mitigated -> monitoring. closing pager but keeping thread open for follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
